heading: Questions? We can read your mind

items.q: What is BBA in Business Psychology?
a: The BBA in Business Psychology at ATLAS ISME equips students with a blend of psychological insight, business acumen and entrepreneurial thinking. The curriculum spans cognitive, business and positive psychology alongside core business competencies, preparing students to understand human behaviour in organisational, consumer and leadership contexts.

items.q: What is the scope of business psychology?
a: The scope is wide and growing. Business Psychology graduates can work across HR, consulting, consumer research, UX, marketing organisational development and leadership coaching. As companies increasingly invest in understanding human behaviour to drive performance and culture, professionals with this dual skill set are in high demand.

Yes. With organisations placing greater emphasis on employee wellbeing, consumer behaviour and people analytics, business psychologists are sought across corporates, start-ups, consultancies and research firms. The combination of psychology and business skills is increasingly rare and valued.

items.q: What's the highest-paid job in psychology?
a: While the website does not specify salary figures, high-paying psychology-adjacent roles in the business world include Organisational Psychologist, People Analytics Lead, Consumer Insights Strategist and UX Researcher, all roles that the ATLAS ISME Business Psychology curriculum prepares students for.

items.q: What careers can I pursue with a BBA in Business Psychology?
a: Graduates are well-prepared for a wide range of careers, including HR & People Analytics, Consumer Behaviour Research organisational Development, Leadership Coaching, Marketing & Brand Strategy, UX Research, Talent Management and Entrepreneurship. The final year includes advanced subjects like Organisational Development, Psychology of Innovation and People Analytics, specifically oriented toward career-readiness.

items.q: Is Business Psychology the same as a Psychology degree?
a: No. A traditional Psychology degree is more clinically and academically oriented. Business Psychology at ATLAS ISME combines psychological theory with business, management and entrepreneurship, making it a career-focused, industry-integrated degree aimed at the corporate and organisational world rather than clinical practice.

items.q: Can Commerce or Science students pursue BBA Business Psychology?
a: Yes. The eligibility requires a minimum of 50% in Class XII in any stream, Commerce, Science or Arts are all accepted. No specific subject background is required, making it accessible to students from all backgrounds who are curious about human behaviour and business.

items.q: What subjects are included in BBA Business Psychology?
a: The curriculum covers Cognitive Psychology, Business Psychology, Positive Psychology, Principles of Management, Marketing Management, Consumer Behaviour, Communication Psychology organisational Behaviour, Behavioural Psychology, Psychology of Innovation, Entrepreneurial Psychology, People Analytics organisational Development, Finance for Enterprise and a Capstone Research Thesis, alongside mandatory internships each semester.

items.q: Is it good to minor in economics?
a: Yes, especially if your major is in a business or strategy-oriented field. The Economics minor at ATLAS ISME helps students explore the economic forces and policies shaping global businesses and markets and learn how economic analysis informs decision-making and drives innovation through public policy. It adds analytical depth and macro-level thinking that directly complements any business major.

items.q: What is a minor subject in BBA?
a: At ATLAS ISME, a minor is a secondary area of specialisation you study alongside your chosen major. The BBA / BBA (Hons.) program is designed in two steps allowing you to design a business education that's as dynamic as the world you're entering. Minors available include Marketing, Finance, Business Analytics, Entrepreneurship, Economics, AI & Emerging Technologies, Digital Branding & Advertising and Business Psychology.

Yes. Economics is not a mandatory standalone subject in the BBA at ATLAS ISME, it is an optional Minor you can choose to add to your degree. If you select a different Minor (such as Finance or Business Analytics), you can still complete your BBA without any Economics coursework. However, a foundational Economics course does appear in the core curriculum as part of the broader business foundation.

They serve different purposes. A BBA is a professional, practice-oriented degree focused on business management, strategy and career readiness across corporate roles. A pure Economics degree is more analytical and research-oriented. At ATLAS ISME, the BBA with an Economics Minor gives you the best of both without committing to a full Economics degree.

At ATLAS ISME, the Economics Minor within the BBA is applied rather than purely mathematical. Subjects include Microeconomic Analysis, Macroeconomic Analysis, Quantitative Methods for Economics, Economic Analysis of Public Policy, International Economics, Development Economics, Behavioural Economics, Game Theory & Strategic Thinking, Environmental & Sustainability Economics and Econometrics & Data Analytics. While some quantitative thinking is involved, the emphasis is on real-world application and business relevance, not advanced pure mathematics.

items.q: What are the subjects in BBA economics?
a: The Economics Minor across the BBA in Marketing curriculum includes: Economics (foundational), Microeconomic Analysis, Macroeconomic Analysis, Quantitative Methods for Economics, Economic Analysis of Public Policy, International Economics, Development Economics, Behavioural Economics, Game Theory & Strategic Thinking, Environmental & Sustainability Economics and Econometrics & Data Analytics.

items.q: Why should a Marketing student choose Economics as a Minor?
a: Economics gives Marketing students a powerful analytical edge. Understanding consumer demand, pricing dynamics, market competition and macroeconomic trends helps marketers build smarter strategies, not just creative ones. Subjects like Behavioural Economics and Game Theory directly enhance how a marketer understands consumer decision-making and competitor behaviour, while Econometrics & Data Analytics adds a quantitative layer to campaign and market analysis.

items.q: How does an Economics Minor enhance career opportunities for students?
a: The Economics Minor equips you with analytical and quantitative skills, helping you understand market trends, economic policies and business environments. This opens doors to roles in market research, economic consulting, policy advisory, finance and strategy. Combining economic insight with your major makes you a well-rounded candidate, giving you an edge in placements and making you highly attractive to recruiters across corporates, start-ups and research institutions.

items.q: Does the Minor in Economics appear on my degree certificate?
a: The website does not specify this directly. It is advisable to confirm with the ATLAS ISME Admissions or Academic team for the exact degree nomenclature. However, at most universities following the NEP framework both the Major and Minor are reflected in the academic transcript and degree documentation.
